## Research Notes
- The doc guards iterate `README.md` and `docs/*.md` non-recursively (`tests/smoke.sh:396,411,435`), so new
  pages are flat: `docs/install-linux.md`, `docs/install-macos.md`, `docs/install-windows.md`,
  `docs/contributing.md`.
- `docs/install.md §N` is cited by number from hooks and the wizard (§5, §7, §7 step 14) — numbering stays.
- The quick-start guard (`tests/smoke.sh:6011-6024`) needs six `## N.` sections and 3–5 steps in §5/§6;
  it also requires `bubblewrap` and `brew install` in the quick start, which this change moves out — the
  guard moves with them (FR-015).
- README guarded strings: footer (release.sh + smoke:116), counts (smoke:2483-2485), `fresh context`
  (smoke:1912), `/hefesto:hef.babysit` (smoke:2883).
- Only README content with no other home: the pane-layout material of "Several sessions, one board"
  (`README.md:233-332`) and the optional-tools list (`README.md:404-407`).

## Data Model
No data model changes required.

## API Contracts
No API changes required. Interface contracts preserved: README footer format, `docs/install.md` §1–§7
numbering, the file names `install.sh` prints (`docs/quickstart.md`, `docs/quickstart.pt-BR.md`,
`docs/install.md`).

## Implementation Approach
1. **Guards first (red).** Edit the quick-start guard and add the front-door guard so they fail against
   today's tree (README is 415 lines, per-OS pages do not exist).
2. **Create the per-OS pages** by moving quick-start §1's table and §2's install paragraph (no rewording
   beyond the move), adding the Windows/WSL page.
3. **Thin the quick starts** (EN then PT, same edit) to hand-overs, keeping six sections and the §5/§6 steps.
4. **Move README-only content** into `docs/install.md` (§7 "Pane layouts", §2 optional tools) before the
   README is cut, so nothing is lost at any commit.
5. **Rewrite README** as the front door; keep every guarded string.
6. **Contributing guide**, citing only what the repo does.
7. **Pointers**: job line + cross-links at the top of quickstart, install.md, SETUP.md.
8. **Verify**: full tier 1 green; run each new guard's mutation; `wc -l README.md`; destination table
   (below) checked heading by heading.

### Sketch 2: Windows page hand-over
**File:** `docs/install-windows.md` (new)
**Intent:** WSL required; no Linux step repeated.

```markdown
# Install on Windows (WSL)
[← back to README](../README.md)
hefesto needs **WSL 2** — its hooks and installer are bash scripts for a Linux or macOS userland; native
Windows is not supported. Install WSL 2 with a Linux distribution following Microsoft's guide
(https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/wsl/install — `wsl --install` in an administrator PowerShell), then
open that distribution's terminal and install Claude Code inside it (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup).
**From here on, follow [Install on Linux](install-linux.md)** in that terminal — every step is the same.
```

**Why this shape:** FR-006; `install.sh:446` has no Windows path; bubblewrap needs WSL 2. Every
Windows-specific step is anchored to Microsoft's or Claude Code's own install page (http links, which the
link guard skips); the page adds no Windows claim of its own beyond "WSL 2 required, native unsupported".

### Sketch 4: guard changes
**File:** `tests/smoke.sh` (modify `:6011-6024`, add a block after it)
**Intent:** move the tool assertions to the pages; pin the front door.

```bash
qs_links() { # <quickstart file> → 0 when it links all three per-OS pages; prints the first missing one
  local p; for p in install-linux install-macos install-windows; do grep -qF "($p.md)" "$1" || { echo "must link $p.md"; return 1; }; done
}
for qs in …quickstart.md …quickstart.pt-BR.md; do
  # …existing checks, minus bubblewrap/brew install…
  qs_msg="$(qs_links "$qs")" || { bad "$(basename "$qs") $qs_msg"; l3_fail=1; }
done
fd_check() { # <root> → 0 when the front door holds; prints the first reason it does not
  local r="$1" n l
  n=$(wc -l < "$r/README.md" | tr -d ' '); [ "$n" -lt 150 ] || { echo "README.md is $n lines (under 150)"; return 1; }
  for l in docs/contributing.md docs/install-linux.md docs/install-macos.md docs/install-windows.md; do
    grep -qF "($l)" "$r/README.md" || { echo "README.md does not link $l"; return 1; }; done
  grep -qF bubblewrap "$r/docs/install-linux.md" && grep -qF 'brew install' "$r/docs/install-macos.md" || { echo "per-OS tools missing"; return 1; }
  grep -qF WSL "$r/docs/install-windows.md" && grep -qF '(install-linux.md)' "$r/docs/install-windows.md" || { echo "Windows page must require WSL and hand over"; return 1; }
}
fd_msg="$(fd_check "$REPO")" || { bad "front door: $fd_msg"; fd_fail=1; }
fd_t="$(mktemp -d)"; fd_copy() { rm -rf "$fd_t/r"; mkdir -p "$fd_t/r/docs"; cp "$REPO/README.md" "$fd_t/r/"; cp "$REPO"/docs/install-*.md "$REPO/docs/contributing.md" "$fd_t/r/docs/"; }
# the pad is a counted loop, not `yes | head` — a SIGPIPE'd producer is the pattern constitution 3 names
fd_copy; i=0; while [ "$i" -lt 150 ]; do echo x; i=$((i + 1)); done >> "$fd_t/r/README.md"
                                                                             fd_check "$fd_t/r" >/dev/null && { bad "mutation survived: a 150-line pad"; fd_fail=1; }
fd_copy; sed -i.bak 's|(docs/contributing.md)||' "$fd_t/r/README.md";        fd_check "$fd_t/r" >/dev/null && { bad "mutation survived: contributing link dropped"; fd_fail=1; }
fd_copy; sed -i.bak 's/WSL/W-S-L/g' "$fd_t/r/docs/install-windows.md";      fd_check "$fd_t/r" >/dev/null && { bad "mutation survived: WSL removed"; fd_fail=1; }
fd_copy; sed -i.bak 's/bubblewrap/bwrap-pkg/g' "$fd_t/r/docs/install-linux.md"; fd_check "$fd_t/r" >/dev/null && { bad "mutation survived: bubblewrap removed"; fd_fail=1; }
cp "$REPO/docs/quickstart.md" "$fd_t/qs.md"; sed -i.bak 's|(install-windows.md)||g' "$fd_t/qs.md"
                                                                             qs_links "$fd_t/qs.md" >/dev/null && { bad "mutation survived: quick start's Windows link dropped"; fd_fail=1; }
rm -rf -- "${fd_t:?}"
```

(`sed -i.bak` with a suffix is the BSD-portable form the macOS guard allows — `tests/smoke.sh:6036`
rejects bare `sed -i` only in hooks, but the suite itself runs on macOS too.)

**Why this shape:** constitution 3 pattern (a) — the check is a function of a root, run on the tree and on
mutated temp copies, as the hook mutations do (`tests/smoke.sh:1254-1258`); the quick-start part keeps
the existing `grep -qF … || { bad; x_fail=1; }` pattern (`tests/smoke.sh:6011-6026`). SC-003 is satisfied
in-suite, so every CI run re-proves the guard can fail.

# Contributing

## Constitution Compliance
- [x] **Principle 1** (payload not under `.claude/`): no payload moves; docs only. The stale-path guard (`smoke.sh:457`) keeps covering every new page.
- [x] **Principle 2** (namespaced commands): every command in new text is `/hefesto:hef.<name>`; `smoke.sh:6436` stays green.
- [x] **Principle 3** (guards mutation-tested): both new checks are functions of their input, run in-suite against mutated temp copies (Sketch 4): `fd_check` against four (150-line pad, contributing link dropped, `WSL` removed, `bubblewrap` removed — the per-OS tool assertions moved out of the quick-start guard), `qs_links` against one (a quick start without its Windows link). Five mutations, each must turn the check red.
- [x] **Principle 4** (zero-install): no tooling added; guards use grep/wc.
- [ ] **Principle 5** (helpers fail loudly): not applicable — no helper changes.

## Risks & Mitigations
| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| A README fact dropped in the cut | lost knowledge | move step (Approach 4) precedes the cut; destination table checked heading by heading (SC-004) |
| A guarded string removed from README or install.md | red CI | run tier 1 after each file; research lists every guarded string |
| Portuguese quick start drifts | US6 fails | same commit edits both; guard loop covers both files |
| `install.md §N` citations shift | wrong pointer in hook messages | no section added before §7; new material is a subsection inside §7 / §2 |
| Windows claims not verifiable on this repo's CI | unverified statement | the page's own claim is only "WSL 2 required, native unsupported" (from `install.sh:446` and the bash hooks); the WSL install steps FR-006 asks for are anchored to Microsoft's WSL install page and Claude Code's setup page |
| Inbound "README §5" citations (`docs/install.md:369,742`, `docs/architecture.md:155`, `docs/performance.md:51`) | point at a section that no longer exists | each becomes a link to `install.md` §7 "Pane layouts"; a final `grep -rn 'README §' docs/ SETUP.md` must return nothing |
| `SETUP.md` orphaned when README `:79-88` is cut | the Claude-guided path disappears | README "Set up a project" keeps the curl prompt; the per-OS pages link `../SETUP.md` |
| README counts drift on next release | red CI | counts stay computed by `smoke.sh:2476-2486` |
